Hi Lucia —

Thanks for outlining the asks. I put together a concise mapping and attached a one-page diagram plus a response matrix that ties SIG questions to evidence examples. High level summary below; full answers and artifacts attached (sig_response_matrix.xlsx, deployment-diagram-hosted-dedicated-private.pdf).

Summary mapping (short):
- Hosted (Redwood-managed):
  - Data plane: customer requests hit Redwood hosted API endpoints; models run on multi-tenant pools we operate.
  - Network isolation: logical isolation via tenancy and VPC egress controls; customers can restrict outbound IPs and use private endpoints in some regions.
  - Encryption at rest: Redwood-managed at rest encryption on object and block stores (customer data tagged and lifecycle-mapped).
  - Key management: Redwood KMS for hosted keys; customers may provide KMS for dedicated/private via integrations (see dedicated/private rows).
  - Access control & audit: Role-based access in Console + token issuance; audit logs stored in Redwood audit pipeline (we provide log extracts for SOC review).

- Dedicated (reserved capacity on Redwood):
  - Data plane: runs in pools dedicated to the customer (no other tenants on GPU hosts); control plane remains Redwood-managed unless Private option chosen.
  - Network isolation: dedicated pools sit in a logically isolated tenant with customer-level network policies; optional IP allowlists.
  - Encryption at rest: customer data on dedicated pools encrypted using either Redwood-managed keys or customer-managed keys (KMS integration).
  - Key management: supports customer KMS (recommended for regulated workloads); we document KMS setup steps in the dedicated onboarding guide.
  - Access control & audit: tenant-level RBAC and token scoping; longer retention options for audit logs available as an add-on.

- Private (VPC / on-prem):
  - Data plane: both control plane and data plane can be placed inside customer-managed network (VPC peering or on-prem deployment), removing Redwood-managed data residency for inference traffic if requested.
  - Network isolation: customer is responsible for network controls inside their VPC/on-prem; Redwood provides deployment templates and hardened images.
  - Encryption at rest: customer-controlled; system can use keys stored in customer KMS/HSM.
  - Key management: customer-managed KMS/HSM by default; Redwood can integrate with vaults and KMS connectors during deployment.
  - Access control & audit: customer-operated IAM for the private deployment; we ship audit hooks and recommend forwarding to customer SIEM.

Artifacts we attached and what they map to in SIG:
- deployment-diagram-hosted-dedicated-private.pdf: high-level network/dataflow diagrams for each mode (useful for SIG DevOps/network questions).
- sig_response_matrix.xlsx: question->answer->evidence mapping (SOC 2 section, diagram page, snippet or configuration sample).

If you want, we can also export a sample SOC 2 control narrative snippet and a redacted audit log extract for the hosted path; for dedicated/private we can provide template KMS configuration and a sample network ACL.

Next steps: tell me which SIG control IDs you want prioritized and we can escalate to Product Security for any deeper artifacts.
